Lisa Ebeling.b:
Northern Colorado named Lisa Ebeling the head coach of the women's swimming and diving program in August of 2016.
Lisa Ebeling has led the Northern Colorado women's swimming and diving program since August of 2016, and in that time she has pushed the Bears to the top half of their conference while building one of the most consistent academic performers in the department.
In the Bears' first year in the Mountain Pacific Sports Federation, Northern Colorado went 6-3 in duals and took third at the MPSF Championships with 1,171.5 points, the highest swimming total at the meet. Maria Erokhina was named MPSF Swimmer of the Year and Ebeling was named MPSF Swimming Coach of the Year, both firsts for the program. Erokhina swept the breaststroke titles, winning the 100 in 59.96 to become the first Bear under one minute and the 200 in 2:10.84, each setting school records and the latter a pool record. Kyra Rabess won the 1650 freestyle in 16:35.33, moving to second all-time, and Ellyson Lombardi won the 200 butterfly in 1:59.70. The Bears set program records in both the 200 and 400 medley relays and a pool record in the 200 freestyle relay. On the boards, Violet Noel broke a decade-old 3-meter record with 332.33 and qualified for NCAA Diving Zone E alongside Mireya Ruiz. Northern Colorado placed eighth at the CSCAA National Invitational Championship with 306.5 points, where Lombardi took second in the 200 butterfly and Avi Tromp broke five Aruban national records. Erokhina closed her season at the NCAA Championships.
The previous season saw Northern Colorado go 4-5 in duals and finish sixth at the WAC Championships with 458.5 points. Madison Berg shattered the program's 1-meter dive record with 309.30, surpassing a mark that had stood since 2011, and was named WAC Diver of the Week twice. The 800 freestyle relay of Rabess, Lora Konter, Martina Yuki Trionfetti and Lily Mayer won gold in 7:14.85, breaking a school record set two years earlier. At the championships, Rabess took bronze in the 1650, Trionfetti third in the 100 freestyle, Erokhina silver in the 200 breaststroke and Lombardi tied for third in the 200 butterfly. Erokhina broke Cyprus national records in the 100 and 200 breaststroke at the Short Course World Championships in Budapest, and Rabess set Cayman Islands records in the 400 and 800 freestyle.
"This team put together an incredible season," said Head Coach Lisa Ebeling. "From setting national records to breaking school records and earning multiple podium finishes at the WAC Championships, our athletes have continued to raise the bar. I'm extremely proud of their dedication and resilience throughout the year."
In 2023-24, the Bears went 3-4 in duals and finished fourth at the WAC Championships with 495 points, recording 21 top-eight finishes, 11 medalists, two champions and three NCAA B-Cut qualifiers. Rabess was named WAC Freshman of the Year. Kyriana Chambo and Berg represented Northern Colorado at the NCAA Zone E Diving Championships, with Chambo placing 34th on the 3-meter and Berg 41st on the 1-meter.
Ebeling's seventh season saw Northern Colorado finish 4-2 in duals and take third at the WAC Championships with 493 points. Twelve swimmers qualified for the CSCAA National Invitational Championships, where the Bears placed 34th, and 16 student-athletes were named to the Winter Academic All-WAC Team.
Ebeling and her team made history in the 2021-22 season, with broken records, wins, and swimmer accolades. They earned three straight WAC dual victories and took down Wyoming for only the second time in program history. They ended the season with an overall record of 9-1 and earned third place at the WAC Championships with the most points in program history, 530.5. At the Championships, the Bears totaled four gold medals, three silver, six bronze, and seven school records. Swimmers Madelyn Moore and Katelyn Bergin also received WAC Swimmer of the Week Honors throughout the season, with Moore also securing WAC Swimmer of the Year for the second consecutive year.
The 2020-21 season also proved to be successful for Ebeling and the Bears as they went on to finish their season with an overall record of 9-1. They also moved up in the WAC standings, tabbing a third place finish at the WAC Championships. Madelyn was also named the WAC Swimmer of the Year. During the season, the program also earned a spot on the Mid-Major Top-25 Ranking for the first time in history, coming in a No. 22.
In 2019-20, Ebeling helped the Bears to 76 lifetime best swims, 35 times the top-10 of program history, three All-WAC First Team members and six All-WAC Second Team members. UNC finished sixth at the WAC Championships, with junior Petra Kis taking home the 400 IM for the second year in a row.
Northern Colorado reached new heights in 2018-19. The team matched its highest ever finish at the WAC Championship by taking third place. In Ebeling's third season as the Bears head coach, the team rewrote the program's record book by breaking 13 records. UNC swam 22 NIC qualifying times and three NCAA B qualifying times over the season as well. At the WAC Championships, Northern Colorado won five titles, including winning three of the five relays, and had 11 swimmers earn either first or second team All-Conference honors.
In 2017-18, the Bears jumped up to a fifth place finish at the WAC Championships and the program won three duel meets against a very tough schedule. The 2017-18 season's top achievement was Petra Kis being named the WAC Freshman of the Year. Kis helped in pushing the team's progress forward as they set six school records and had four NCAA B qualifying times.
In her first season with Northern Colorado, the team won six duel meets and finished seventh in the WAC with a strong final day at the WAC Championship. Over the year one program record was broke, but the foundation was laid for the years to come for the program.

Kyle Ponsler.b:
Head swimming & diving coach, Lisa Ebeling has announced the addition of Kyle Ponsler to the Northern Colorado swimming & diving staff in July of 2026. Ponsler will serve as an assistant coach for the Bears.
Ponsler came to UNC straight out of the pool at North Carolina State where he spent two years as a captain.
During his career at NC State he accumulated a long list of accomplishments:
• 2025 NCAA Championships – Posted the 4th fastest time in the NCAA & set the all-time NC State school record in the 400 IM (3:37.42), also personal best in the 200 Backstroke, 3-time ACC Finalist (500 free, 400 IM, Mile), ACC All-Academic Team
• 2024 400 IM ACC Champion – First Wolfpack man since 2018 to win the 400 IM (3:41.18), 3-time ACC Finalist (500 Free, 400IM, Mile), Broke NC State 400 IM record at NCAA Championship posting 3:39.28 in Finals (6th fastest NCAA time of the year)
• 2024 U.S. Olympic Trials Finalist – 6th in the 400m IM (4:16.53); PBs in 200m Back (1:59.74) and 200m IM (2:02.55).
• 2023 World University Games – Represented Team USA in the 400 IM and 200 IM in Chengdu, China, 3-time ACC Finalist (200 IM, 400 IM, 200 Back), qualified/selected for NCAA Championships (400 IM), ACC All-Academic Team
• 2023 NC State "Bell Tower" award winner (Freshman that made the biggest impact) followed by 2024 "Most Improved", and voted Team Caption for 2025 & 2026
• 2022 - 2x USA National JR Team, 2x NCSA National Champion (200 IM & 400 IM)/Broke Meet Record (400 IM)
• 2022 IHSAA 500 Freestyle Champion, 3x Indiana State Championship Finalist (2022), 14x IHSAA State Finalist, Academic All-American, 2022 Gene Lee Outstanding Athlete Award Winner (Indiana Swimming).
• 2021 Wave 1 Olympic Trials Runner up, 2021 USA World Cup Team/International JR team
• 2019 Toyota US Open Champion (400 IM), Silver Medalist Winter Junior National Championships (400 IM), 2019 Central Zone & National Select Camp participant (USA Swimming)
Ponsler also competed in four World Cups, two World University Games, and two Open Water World Cups.
